use: For a warm, settled happiness about your life or a moment.

example.romaji: oishii mono tabeteru toki ga ichiban shiawase
example.ja: おいしいもの食べてる時が一番幸せ
example.english: I'm happiest when I'm eating something good.

examplePolite.romaji: oishii mono o tabete iru toki ga ichiban shiawase desu
examplePolite.ja: おいしいものを食べている時が一番幸せです
examplePolite.english: I'm happiest when I'm eating something good.

notes: Glad about one specific thing (good news, a gift) is ureshii, not shiawase.

use: Heavier than arigatou: deep thanks, often to family or for long-term help.

example.romaji: oya ni wa hontou ni kansha shiteru
example.ja: 親には本当に感謝してる
example.english: I'm really grateful to my parents.

examplePolite.romaji: ryoushin ni wa hontou ni kansha shite imasu
examplePolite.ja: 両親には本当に感謝しています
examplePolite.english: I'm truly grateful to my parents.

notes: Grateful to someone: [person] ni kansha suru. Kansha shika nai = I can't thank you enough.

use: The smile as a thing someone has; the verb 'to smile' is warau.

example.romaji: ano ko, egao ga kawaii yo ne
example.ja: あの子、笑顔がかわいいよね
example.english: She's got a cute smile, hasn't she?

examplePolite.romaji: ano kata wa egao ga suteki desu ne
examplePolite.ja: あの方は笑顔がすてきですね
examplePolite.english: She has a lovely smile, doesn't she?

notes: Egao de = with a smile. Egao ni naru = break into a smile.

use: Big-picture hope (there's still hope), and in bookings or shops, what you'd prefer.

example.romaji: mada kibou wa aru yo
example.ja: まだ希望はあるよ
example.english: There's still hope.

examplePolite.romaji: mada kibou wa arimasu yo
examplePolite.ja: まだ希望はありますよ
examplePolite.english: There's still hope.

notes: Kibou no jikan = the time you'd like (for a delivery or booking). For personal dreams, people often say yume.

use: Said when a worry lifts; anshin shite (don't worry) reassures someone.

example.romaji: buji de yokatta, anshin shita yo
example.ja: 無事でよかった、安心したよ
example.english: I'm so glad you're safe. What a relief.

examplePolite.romaji: buji de yokatta desu, anshin shimashita
examplePolite.ja: 無事でよかったです、安心しました
examplePolite.english: I'm so glad you're safe. What a relief.

notes: Opposite: fuan (anxious). Hotto suru is a softer 'feel relieved'.

use: A nagging worry about what's coming, not sudden fear.

example.romaji: ashita no mensetsu, chotto fuan
example.ja: 明日の面接、ちょっと不安
example.english: I'm a bit nervous about tomorrow's interview.

examplePolite.romaji: ashita no mensetsu ga chotto fuan desu
examplePolite.ja: 明日の面接がちょっと不安です
examplePolite.english: I'm a bit nervous about tomorrow's interview.

notes: Fuan ni naru = start to worry. Shinpai is worry about a specific thing or person; fuan is a general uneasy feeling.

use: Often as a jab: kore de manzoku? (Happy now?).

example.romaji: kono kekka ni wa manzoku shiteru
example.ja: この結果には満足してる
example.english: I'm happy with how this turned out.

examplePolite.romaji: kono kekka ni wa manzoku shite imasu
examplePolite.ja: この結果には満足しています
examplePolite.english: I'm happy with how this turned out.

notes: Opposite: fuman. Also a na-adjective: manzoku na kekka (a satisfying result).

use: A grievance you hold; most often fuman ga aru (have a complaint).

example.romaji: nanka fuman de mo aru no?
example.ja: なんか不満でもあるの?
example.english: Got a problem with that?

examplePolite.romaji: nani ka fuman de mo arimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 何か不満でもありますか?
examplePolite.english: Is there something you're unhappy with?

notes: Opposite: manzoku. Fumansou na kao = a disgruntled look.

use: A flat brush-off: [thing] ni kyoumi nai.

example.romaji: sonna hanashi, kyoumi nai yo
example.ja: そんな話、興味ないよ
example.english: I'm not interested in that kind of thing.

examplePolite.romaji: sou iu hanashi ni wa kyoumi arimasen
examplePolite.ja: そういう話には興味ありません
examplePolite.english: I'm not interested in that kind of thing.

notes: Positive: kyoumi ga aru (be interested). Said about a person, it sounds cold.

use: Romantic love as a topic or part of life, not a feeling toward one person.

example.romaji: ima wa ren'ai yori shigoto ga daiji
example.ja: 今は恋愛より仕事が大事
example.english: Right now work matters more than romance.

examplePolite.romaji: ima wa ren'ai yori shigoto ga daiji desu
examplePolite.ja: 今は恋愛より仕事が大事です
examplePolite.english: Right now work matters more than romance.

notes: Loving one person is suki or koi. Ren'ai kekkon = a love marriage.

use: What you like in food, style or people: watashi no konomi (my type).

example.romaji: kare, kanzen ni watashi no konomi
example.ja: 彼、完全に私の好み
example.english: He's totally my type.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa kanzen ni watashi no konomi desu
examplePolite.ja: 彼は完全に私の好みです
examplePolite.english: He's totally my type.

notes: Konomi ja nai = not my thing. For people, taipu is just as common.

use: Jealousy in love, and envy of someone's success.

example.romaji: betsu ni shitto shitenai shi
example.ja: 別に嫉妬してないし
example.english: It's not like I'm jealous or anything.

examplePolite.romaji: betsu ni shitto shite imasen yo
examplePolite.ja: 別に嫉妬していませんよ
examplePolite.english: I'm not jealous, you know.

notes: Casual alternative: yakimochi o yaku. Urayamashii is the lighter 'I envy you'.

english: when I was a kid; childhood
use: The standard opener for a childhood memory.

example.romaji: kodomo no koro, yoku koko de asonda
example.ja: 子供の頃、よくここで遊んだ
example.english: When I was a kid, I played here a lot.

examplePolite.romaji: kodomo no koro, yoku koko de asobimashita
examplePolite.ja: 子供の頃、よくここで遊びました
examplePolite.english: When I was a kid, I played here a lot.

notes: Kodomo no koro kara = ever since I was a kid. Chiisai koro means the same.

use: A soft, everyday way to talk about early childhood.

example.romaji: chiisai koro wa yasai kirai datta
example.ja: 小さい頃は野菜嫌いだった
example.english: I hated vegetables when I was little.

examplePolite.romaji: chiisai koro wa yasai ga kirai deshita
examplePolite.ja: 小さい頃は野菜が嫌いでした
examplePolite.english: I hated vegetables when I was little.

notes: Same as kodomo no koro. Chiisai here means young, not small.

use: Points to a time both of you know, often with nostalgia.

example.romaji: ano koro wa tanoshikatta na
example.ja: あの頃は楽しかったな
example.english: Those were good times.

examplePolite.romaji: ano koro wa tanoshikatta desu ne
examplePolite.ja: あの頃は楽しかったですね
examplePolite.english: Those were good times, weren't they?

notes: Sono koro = at that time, in a story you're telling the listener.

use: Sets the scene when explaining past events: touji wa, touji no ~ (the ~ of that time).

example.romaji: touji wa mada gakusei datta
example.ja: 当時はまだ学生だった
example.english: I was still a student at the time.

examplePolite.romaji: touji wa mada gakusei deshita
examplePolite.ja: 当時はまだ学生でした
examplePolite.english: I was still a student at the time.

notes: More factual than ano koro. Don't mix it up with toujitsu (on the day).

use: A fond memory of something you did or lived through, not the ability to remember.

example.romaji: ii omoide ni natta ne
example.ja: いい思い出になったね
example.english: That turned into a nice memory, didn't it?

examplePolite.romaji: ii omoide ni narimashita ne
examplePolite.ja: いい思い出になりましたね
examplePolite.english: That turned into a nice memory, didn't it?

notes: What your brain stores is kioku. Omoidasu = to remember, recall.

use: What you can recall: kioku ga nai (I don't remember), kioku o ushinau (lose your memory).

example.romaji: sono hi no kioku ga zenzen nai
example.ja: その日の記憶が全然ない
example.english: I have no memory of that day at all.

examplePolite.romaji: sono hi no kioku ga zenzen arimasen
examplePolite.ja: その日の記憶が全然ありません
examplePolite.english: I have no memory of that day at all.

notes: A cherished memory is omoide. Kiokuryoku = memory as a skill.

use: Opens a story about a past day; not for a future 'someday'.

example.romaji: aru hi, kyuu ni kare kara denwa ga kita
example.ja: ある日、急に彼から電話が来た
example.english: Then one day he suddenly called me.

examplePolite.romaji: aru hi, kyuu ni kare kara denwa ga kimashita
examplePolite.ja: ある日、急に彼から電話が来ました
examplePolite.english: Then one day he suddenly called me.

notes: Someday in the future is itsuka. Aru means 'a certain', as in aru hito (someone).

use: Any happening, big or small: kyou no dekigoto (what happened today).

example.romaji: ano dekigoto wa ima demo wasurerarenai
example.ja: あの出来事は今でも忘れられない
example.english: I still can't forget what happened that time.

examplePolite.romaji: ano dekigoto wa ima demo wasureraremasen
examplePolite.ja: あの出来事は今でも忘れられません
examplePolite.english: I still can't forget what happened that time.

notes: In casual speech people often just say koto: hen na koto ga atta. A planned event is ibento.
